CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling in both hands.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 60-year-old right-handed male presenting with numbness and tingling in both hands for a few weeks, which worsened over the last month. Symptoms began following a car accident in December when patient sustained bilateral wrist fractures. Right wrist was more severely injured than left. Patient reports symptoms extend from the middle and ring finger up the forearm on the right side, and from the pinky and ring finger on the left side. Symptoms are primarily soreness with occasional throbbing and associated weakness, especially with use. Tingling is more pronounced when pain is present and becomes dull when pain resolves. Symptoms occur mainly at night and come and go throughout the day. Patient denies loss of sensation but reports decreased sensitivity. Patient also reports mild neck stiffness since hitting head during accident with diagnosed contusion. Patient wears splints on both wrists, with right wrist splinting being more consistent. Patient was prescribed nerve pain medication but reports non-compliance with taking it as directed.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: Fatigue and weight gain. GI: Excessive appetite and bloating. Eyes: Floaters. Cardiovascular: Shortness of breath and leg swelling. Endocrine: Persistent hunger. Skin: Nail bed changes, dryness, and itching. Musculoskeletal: Gout and muscle pain. Remainder of review of systems: Negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Bilateral wrist fractures from car accident in December. Head contusion from same accident. Prediabetes, currently controlled with diet modification. Hypertension. Anxiety.

MEDICATIONS
Coreg for hypertension. Lexapro for anxiety. Nerve pain medication (patient non-compliant).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurologic examination: Pin prick sensation diminished in third and fourth fingers on right hand. Sensation decreased in fourth and fifth fingers on left hand. Reflexes 1+ and symmetric in upper extremities; 2+ at knees; toes downgoing bilaterally. Tinel sign positive at both wrists and both elbows. Rest of examination normal.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, likely secondary to bilateral wrist trauma from motor vehicle accident. Differential includes bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome. Plan: Schedule EMG test to measure nerve responsiveness and pinpoint location of nerve irritation. Patient to continue wearing splints on both wrists. Follow-up visit after testing to review results. If symptoms persist, consider referral to hand clinic for possible injections or carpal tunnel release surgery, or referral to orthopedist for same treatment options.
